result.rationale: The diff in GoogleCalendarService deleteEvent changes the fallback from `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (old) to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` — but the find only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the comparison against a falsy value can never match and always yields undefined. Unlike updateEvent where `selectedCalendar || "primary"` exists, deleteEvent passes this undefined calendarId straight to `calendar.events.delete`, so a delete whose reference lacks externalCalendarId targets the wrong/no calendar instead

judged_text: deleteEvent has the same dead fallback: `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy and compares against that falsy value, so it never matches and the intended destination-calendar fallback is unreachable. Cancellation of a booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId resolves calendarId to undefined (falling back to 'primary') instead of the calendar the event was created in, leaving the original calendar event orphaned and its slot busy.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` compute the fallback calendar ID as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. Because the `find(...)` branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, it compares `cal.externalId` to a falsy/undefined `externalCalendarId`, which will not match a real externalId. This makes the intended destination-calendar fallback effectively unreachable and can yield `undefined` for the calendar id when `externalCalendarId` is missing, unlike the previous logic which used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` directly.
